newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex sees demerger boosting both units.
newsitem.headline: Vendex sees demerger boosting both units.

text.p: Vendex chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels is confident the planned demerger of the Dutch group's services activities from its retailing core will work out positively for both segments.
"After the demerger, both companies will have a very strong position for further growth," Vendex chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said.
Vendex earlier today said it intended to place and list shares worth 600 million guilders of the new services group Vedior N.V. by an initial public offering in the middle of 1997.
The amount of the placement was a result of Vendex's goal to start with two healthy companies, both able to live independently, and with a debtless services arm, he said.
"The outcome was we needed an additional 600 million guilders, which seems a reasonable amount to me," Hessels said.
He said more information on the transaction and the valuation of the new shares would be made available in a prospectus, likely to be published in the second half of May.
Vendex's current shareholders will receive the remaining Vedior N.V. shares, as soon as technically possible after the IPO, he said.
This would likely take around 90 days, he added.
He said the demerger was going according to the plan, but the company was still awaiting government approval of the law permitting such operations.

"We expect the split-up to be finalised at the beginning of 1998, depending on the moment at which changes in the law on the split up of legal entities will become valid, or the obtaining of an earlier ruling by the Ministry of Finance," Vendex earlier said in a statement.
The legal and other steps needed for the demerger have to be approved at the general shareholders meeting in May.
Hessels said the demerger would help Vendex's food retail unit pursue further acquisitions.
"There's only a limited number of players on the market. We are now better positioned for further growth."
The acquisition policy of the retail arm was focused on the food sector, mainly in the Netherlands, he added.

The group recently strengthened its foothold in the specialty stores segment with the acquisition of sports footware and clothing chain Scapino and the opticians chain of the Optische Exploitatie Maatschappij.
Retail and services group Vendex earlier on Tuesday announced a 30 percent rise in 1996/97 total net profit to 539 million guilders.
The services arm made an operating profit of 129 million guilders, up from 115 million in 1995/96. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
